neighbours.label: a preposition (to / at / in) that introduces the place a voyage, flight or historical event reaches or happens at
fire: In 1851 the clipper made the passage from Boston to San Francisco in under ninety days.
The armistice was signed at Compiegne in a railway carriage.
The fleet anchored at Tahiti for two weeks to take on fresh water.
The raiders struck the harbour at Pearl Harbor early on Sunday morning.
Their airship flew from Friedrichshafen to Lakehurst without stopping.
The expedition wintered at Hobart before sailing for the ice.
The congress met at Vienna to redraw the map of Europe.
After the storm the whaler limped into port at Nantucket.
quiet: In 1851 the clipper made the passage in under ninety days, a new record.
The armistice was signed at dawn in a railway carriage.
The fleet anchored for two weeks to take on fresh water.
The raiders struck the harbour at first light early on Sunday morning.
Their airship flew to its full height without stopping.
The expedition rested for a month before sailing for the ice.
The congress met to redraw the map of Europe.
After the storm the whaler limped back with a broken mast.

notes: card: top peaks ' at', ' in', ' to', ' from' before Hawaii, Paris, Tokyo, Suratte; - pole is the same slot before Palestine/Israel/Poland. Probes uneven: 'signed at Versailles' 0.49, 'Liverpool to New York' 0.25, others 0.05-0.10. Near misses: the same prepositions before a time, person or object instead of a place.
